title: Hatred and jealousy
intro: Hatred and jealousy are illnesses of the heart – and a Muslim works to keep the heart clean.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) teaches us to seek refuge with Him from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers evil thoughts into people’s hearts. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nas 114:4–5)</small>

Hatred is a negative feeling that first appears in people’s hearts, and then shows in how they behave towards the people they hate. Hatred is the result of long-lasting anger towards someone and the wish to harm them – their honour, their good name or their belongings. It usually appears when we could not let out our anger at that person. Often we hate someone for no reason at all, which is never good.
Shaytan wants to put hatred and other bad qualities into the hearts of believers, because they spoil how we treat others and break the unity of Muslims.

It is the duty of every Muslim to notice Shaytan’s whispering and to throw out of their heart even the smallest feeling of hatred. By working on the purity of our soul and heart, we can protect ourselves from the illness of hatred.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “The illness of the nations before you has crept up on you: envy and hatred. Hatred is a razor – not a razor that shaves hair, but a razor that shaves away faith.” (Tirmidhi)

Hatred can take over the heart of one person, and also the hearts of a whole Muslim community. In the first case it ruins the faith of the person; in the second it breaks the unity of the whole community. Its three most common results are:

items: it brings disunity among Muslims – the worst and most dangerous thing for a community is when Muslims turn away from each other,
it harms health – when a person led by hatred cannot get what they want, it affects their health.

learn.html: A believer must never be happy about someone else’s misfortune, or say they are glad something bad happened to someone.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “You will not enter Jannah until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread salam among yourselves.” (Muslim)

Besides hatred, jealousy is a big danger to a person’s iman. Jealousy is not only a sin – it is also a kind of very harmful illness of the soul. It is born in the heart, and if it is given a reason, it leads a person into deeds that Islam forbids.

It is told that the wise Luqman worked as a servant for a rich man. The man told him to slaughter a sheep and bring him its two best parts. Luqman brought the tongue and the heart. Then the man told him to slaughter another sheep and bring its two worst parts – and again Luqman brought the tongue and the heart.

Surprised, the rich man asked: “I asked you for the two best parts and you brought the tongue and the heart, and then for the two worst parts and you brought the tongue and the heart again – why?” Luqman answered: “Truly, there is nothing better than the tongue and the heart when they are good, and nothing worse than them when they are bad.”

practice.title: What hatred does
practice.prompt: Tap the three results of hatred the book lists, then tap Check.

options.text: 🧩 It breaks the unity of Muslims

options.why: Hatred breaks unity – spreading salam is what brings people closer.
When a person led by hatred can’t get what they want, it hurts their health and peace.

practice.title: Luqman’s lesson
practice.prompt: Put the story in the right order.
items: The rich man asks for the two best parts of a sheep
Luqman brings the tongue and the heart
The rich man asks for the two worst parts
Luqman brings the tongue and the heart again
Luqman explains: nothing is better when they are good, nothing worse when they are bad

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) compare hatred to?
options: A razor that shaves away faith

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) tell us to do so that we love one another?
Who wants to put hatred into the believers’ hearts?
Which two parts did Luqman bring both times?
